startup.downloading: First launch: downloading the JPL DE440 ephemeris (32 MB)…

side.datetime_tip: Date and time in Universal Time; the arrow opens the calendar
side.place_tip: Type the name of a city and pick it: latitude, longitude and elevation are filled in (cities over 15,000 inhabitants, GeoNames, offline). "Paris, US" for a country.
side.latitude_tip: Decimal degrees, positive north (48.85 for Paris)
side.longitude_tip: Decimal degrees, positive east (2.35 for Paris)
side.geoloc_tip: Detect my position (the device's location service, else the IP address)
side.timezone_tip: IANA time zone, summer time included; type to search ("Paris", "Kolkata"…). "Automatic" uses the place's zone
side.elevation_tip: Observer's height above the horizon (m): it lowers the horizon, so the rise comes earlier and the set later
side.calculate_tip: Calculate for the date and place entered ({key})
side.live_tip: Follow the current time, updated automatically ({key})

coordinates.note_cartesian_heliocentric: x, y, z and distance: from the Sun's centre, ecliptic and equinox J2000, geometric positions (as JPL Horizons); x towards the equinox, z towards the ecliptic pole.
coordinates.note_cartesian_geocentric: x, y, z and distance: from the Earth's centre, true ecliptic of date, apparent positions; x towards the equinox, z towards the ecliptic pole.
coordinates.note_cartesian_topocentric: x, y, z and distance: from the place, true ecliptic of date, apparent positions; x towards the equinox, z towards the ecliptic pole.
coordinates.note_angular_equatorial: Angles: right ascension and declination seen from the place (apparent, true equinox of date).
coordinates.note_angular_horizontal: Angles: azimuth (from the north through the east) and altitude seen from the place, without refraction.
coordinates.note_angular_ecliptic_sun: Angles: ecliptic longitude and latitude seen from the Sun (J2000).
coordinates.note_angular_ecliptic_earth: Angles: ecliptic longitude and latitude seen from the Earth (apparent, true equinox of date).
coordinates.note_observation: Magnitude, Sun angle and constellation: seen from the Earth.

eclipse_map.button_tip: The eclipse projected on the ground
eclipse_map.title: {eclipse} {type} — greatest on {date}
eclipse_map.limits: Limits at the start and end of the partial phase
eclipse_map.note_solar: Band: the Moon's umbra (or antumbra) on the ground, minute by minute; curves: maximum magnitude of the partiality, Sun up. JPL DE440, WGS84 ellipsoid.
eclipse_map.note_lunar: Light zone: the Moon is up at greatest eclipse; dashes: limit of the Moon being up at the start and end of the partial (or penumbral) phase.

event_map.button_tip: Paths of the bodies among the stars around the event
event_map.title: {event} — {date}
event_map.note: Equatorial coordinates of date: north up, east left, as in the sky. Small dots: positions at regular intervals, dated in Universal Time; large dot: position at the instant of the event. For the Moon: positions every 6 hours over two days.

status.invalid_coords: Invalid coordinates: latitude between −90 and 90, longitude between −180 and 180.

planets.group_minor_tip: Ceres, Pallas, Juno, Vesta, the dwarf planets Pluto, Eris, Haumea and Makemake, and Sedna (JPL positions)
planets.visible_only_tip: Only the bodies above the horizon at the computed instant; click a header to sort
planets.sorted_ascending: Sorted in ascending order (click to reverse)
planets.sorted_descending: Sorted in descending order (click to reverse)

chart.trajectory_title: Altitude of the Sun and the Moon — {date}
chart.hint: Hover over the curves to read the altitude at any time. The background follows the Sun's altitude: day, twilights, night.

skymap.title: Sky map — {datetime} UT
skymap.mag_tip: Stars fainter than this magnitude are hidden
skymap.hint: Zenith at the centre, horizon on the circle. Hover over an object to identify it, click to open its card.

detail.title: Details — {name}
detail.click_tip: Click a body to open its data window

events.click_to_search: Pick a search above: it starts from the date entered in the sidebar.
events.no_conjunction: No event in this period with these filters.
events.eclipse_note: Time of greatest eclipse, in Universal Time.
events.precise_note: Times in Universal Time, to the minute (JPL DE440, apparent positions seen from the Earth's centre). Conjunction: same ecliptic longitude; opposition: 180° from the Sun. Visibility from the chosen place in the night of the event: body at least 5° high, Sun 6° below the horizon (12° for the minor planets). Meteor showers: peak from the IMO calendar, radiant at least 5° high, Sun 12° below the horizon.
events.conjunction_inferior: {planet} at inferior conjunction with the Sun
events.conjunction_superior: {planet} at superior conjunction with the Sun
events.export_tip: Save the events shown to a calendar (iCalendar)
events.visible_evening: Visible in the evening: {alt}° above the horizon, towards {dir}, at {time}
events.visible_morning: Visible in the morning: {alt}° above the horizon, towards {dir}, at {time}
events.visible_night: Visible all night: highest at {alt}°, towards {dir}, at {time}
events.invisible_daylight: Not observable from here: up by day only
events.invisible_horizon: Not observable from here: below the horizon at night
events.invisible_no_night: Not observable from here: no dark night
events.local_sun_down: Here: the Sun is down during the whole eclipse
events.local_moon_down: Here: the Moon is down during the whole eclipse
events.local_moon_partly: Moon up during part of the eclipse only

meteors.title: Peak of the {name}
meteors.best: Best around {time}: radiant {alt}° high, towards {dir}, up to {rate} meteors per hour under a dark sky

favs.none_selected: Choose a favourite in the list first.

errors.geoloc_ip: Approximate position from the IP address: {city}, {country} — often the Internet provider's. Turn on the system's location service, or enter your coordinates.
errors.geoloc_network:
Cannot reach the geolocation service. Check your connection.

Detail: {detail}
errors.geoloc_ip_short: Approximate position from the IP address: {city}, {country} (often the internet provider's).
errors.geoloc_reason_no_source: No location service is available on this device. Enter your coordinates, or choose a favourite.
errors.geoloc_reason_access: Windows denies Céleste the position. In Settings › Privacy & security › Location, turn on “Location services” and “Let desktop apps access your location”, then try again.
errors.geoloc_reason_closed: The device's location service is turned off. Turn it on in the system settings, then try again.
errors.geoloc_reason_timeout: The location service found no position within 15 s (Wi-Fi off, computer without GPS or Wi-Fi?). Check that it is on, then try again.
errors.geoloc_reason_invalid: The location service answered without a valid position.
errors.geoloc_reason_unknown: The location service reported an error.

settings.angle_format_tip: Angle format in the whole application; the Coordinates tab can have its own
settings.use_current_tip: Saves the name above with the coordinates and time zone entered in the sidebar
settings.reset_confirm: Restore all default settings (theme, language, startup location, live mode)?
settings.about: Céleste {version} computes the positions of the Sun, the Moon, the planets and the minor planets with the JPL DE440 and JPL Horizons ephemerides. Settings and favourites are in the .celeste folder of your profile.
settings.theme_hint: Choose the theme at the bottom of the sidebar: Night, Day or Observation (red on black, for observing outdoors at night).
settings.reset_hint: Restores the theme, language, time format, startup location and live mode to their original values. Favourites are kept.
settings.credits: Astræos design. IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono fonts (OFL licence), Astraeos Symboles after Noto Sans Symbols (OFL licence). Material Design Icons (Apache 2.0 licence). Cities of the place search: GeoNames (CC BY 4.0 licence).

theme.observation_tip: Red on black, to keep your night vision outdoors

links.feature_tip: An idea for Céleste, on GitHub
links.body_tip: A body to add to Céleste (minor planet, comet, star…), on GitHub
